sources.entry: Do you have an SRE team yet? How to start and assess your journey

summary.name: Google Cloud SRE Team Checklists
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog post by Gustavo Franco offering checklists for assessing how far a team has progressed toward a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) model, from beginner to advanced.
use_cases: assess how mature an existing SRE team is
plan steps to move a team toward an SRE model
benchmark SRE practices against industry checklists
decide what to read next in the SRE Workbook
check whether an SRE team is healthy and sustainable
summary.what_it_does: The post presents three checklists of SRE practices ordered by team maturity: just getting started, beginner SRE teams, intermediate SRE teams, and advanced SRE teams. Items cover SLOs, blameless postmortems, incident management, canary releases, rollback, runbooks, disaster recovery testing, toil levels, and on-call load. It also lists less common features such as geographically distributed SRE teams and separate reporting chains. The author suggests next steps like reading the SRE Workbook chapters in order and contacting an account manager about CRE involvement for Google Cloud customers.
notable: Tiered checklists (just starting, beginner, intermediate, advanced) for judging SRE team maturity
Explicitly states SRE is not dependent on using Google Cloud
Links to chapters of The Site Reliability Workbook, now available in HTML
caveats: The checklists are non-exhaustive and described as one view, not a canonical standard
Access to Customer Reliability Engineer (CRE) involvement is only for GCP customers and requires applying through an account manager
